obligation: FSMA intentional adulteration rule (food defense)
basis: Part 121 applies to facilities required to register under FD&C Act section 415 (21 CFR 121.1). Farms do not register (21 CFR 1.226(b)); the 48 farms are primary production farms and the 3 hubs are secondary activities farms under 21 CFR 1.227, and farm activities subject to the Produce Safety standards are exempt (121.5(d)). The very small business exemption (121.5(a)) does not apply at this size, so farm status is the condition that would change the answer. Confirmed in counsel review and the 2026-07 applicability memo. Used only as a voluntary checklist for fertigation tampering

obligation: Farm status of the regional hubs (secondary activities farm)
basis: A hub stays a secondary activities farm only while company farms grow the majority of what it packs and holds. Hub shares 2026 year to date are 22%, 31% and 18%; the grower services plan would take Hub 2 above a majority in 2027, which would require FDA registration and bring Parts 121 and 117 into scope

obligation: Reportable Food Registry
basis: The duty falls on the responsible party that registers a food facility; the company registers none. Kept in the P08 matrix for coordination with buyers

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents)
basis: Publicly traded SEC registrant, not a smaller reporting company. Item 106 defines information systems to include physical infrastructure controlled by them, so irrigation and packing OT are in scope. Confirmed in counsel review

obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 (risk management, strategy and governance)
basis: Same registrant status; the FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; IT general controls over ERP and payroll (SYS-11) are tested by the SOX program and are not repeated in these deliverables

obligation: Produce Safety Rule record requirements
basis: Covered farm: produce sales far exceed the inflation-adjusted $25,000 threshold (112.4(a)), and food sales far exceed the qualified exemption limit (112.5). Peanuts and sweet corn are rarely consumed raw, and cotton and field corn are not produce. Only the Subpart O record duties are analyzed

obligation: Food Traceability Rule
basis: The company grows, cools and initially packs foods on the Food Traceability List (tomatoes, peppers, cucumbers, melons). The farm alternative to the sortable spreadsheet (1.1455(c)(3)(iii)(A), no more than $250,000 a year) does not apply. Pub. L. 119-37 directed FDA not to enforce the rule before 2028-07-20

obligation: H-2A earnings records and hours and earnings statements
basis: About 5,600 H-2A workers under about 60 labor certifications a year

obligation: Worker Protection Standard application and hazard information
basis: Agricultural employer applying pesticides on its establishments; application records are kept in the FMIS

obligation: FAA Part 107 small unmanned aircraft rules
basis: About 140 company drones flown by about 58 certificated remote pilots

obligation: FAA Part 137 agricultural aircraft operations
basis: The company flies no application aircraft; contracted applicators must hold Part 137 certificates, checked at vendor onboarding

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (data security, breach notification, disposal; worked example)
basis: The company holds personal information of Florida residents: workers, growers and produce box subscribers. Florida is the worked example for the state of residence analysis

obligation: Breach notification and data security laws of other states
citation: Statutes of Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina and each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Operations in 4 states; seasonal and H-2A workers add home-country addresses and temporary housing to the residence analysis

obligation: State comprehensive consumer privacy laws
citation: State statutes, including the Florida Digital Bill of Rights
basis: None is enacted in Georgia, South Carolina or North Carolina according to the repository's cross-sector register (as of 2026-09-25). Florida's Digital Bill of Rights is reported to reach only businesses with more than $1 billion in revenue that also meet further criteria; that threshold was not verified and is flagged for counsel. Subscribers are only in Florida and Georgia

obligation: PCI DSS merchant validation (by contract)
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1; acquirer merchant agreement
basis: Acquirer agreement for the produce box requires an annual self-assessment questionnaire; the hosted payment page keeps card data off company systems

obligation: HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The company is not a covered entity or a business associate; the employee group health plan is a separate covered entity handled by the benefits program and is outside these deliverables

obligation: Federal contract clauses (basic safeguarding, Kaspersky, covered telecommunications)
basis: No federal prime contracts or subcontracts since the company stopped bidding on USDA commodity purchases in 2024

obligation: Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act
basis: Final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. As proposed, it would cover the company through the size criterion, because revenue exceeds the SBA size standard for NAICS 111998 ($2.5 million, 13 CFR 121.201)

obligation: Sanctions screening before any ransom payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; the cyber policy also requires insurer approval before any ransom payment

obligation: Retail and foodservice supplier agreements (24-hour notice, audits, traceability labels, EDI)
basis: About 76% of revenue is under these agreements; they require notice within 24 hours of events affecting product safety, lot traceability or committed volumes

obligation: Client agreements for SL-1 and SL-2 (assurance reports, availability, confidentiality and notice)
citation: SL-1 client agreements; SL-2 grower agreements
basis: SL-1 clients receive an annual SOC 2 Type 2 report and notice within 72 hours; SL-2 growers rely on lot codes and traceability data

obligation: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with SP 800-82 Rev. 3 for OT
basis: No binding sector-specific federal cybersecurity rule applies to primary agricultural production; CSF 2.0 is the sector-neutral baseline named in the industry profile
